tools.name: alert_rule_add
tools.title: Alert Rule Add
tools.description: Add a new alert rule to LibreNMS.

payload.description:
Alert rule payload fields:
- name (required): Rule name
- builder (required): Rule builder JSON with conditions
- devices (required): Array of device IDs or [-1] for all devices
- severity (required): ok, warning, critical
- count (optional): Trigger threshold count (default: 1)
- delay (optional): Delay before alerting in seconds
- interval (optional): Re-alert interval in seconds
- mute (optional): Mute alerts (true/false)
- invert (optional): Invert rule logic (true/false)
- notes (optional): Rule notes
- disabled (optional): Disable rule (0/1)

Do not include rule_id: LibreNMS would edit that rule instead of adding one.

Example:
{"name": "Device Down", "severity": "critical", "devices": [-1], "builder": {"condition": "AND", "rules": [...]}}

payload.description:
Alert rule edit payload (must include rule_id field):
- rule_id (required): Integer rule ID to edit. Without it LibreNMS would create a new
  rule, so the tool refuses the call.
- name: Rule name
- builder: Rule builder JSON with conditions
- devices: Array of device IDs or [-1] for all devices
- severity: ok, warning, critical
- count: Trigger threshold count
- delay: Delay before alerting in seconds
- interval: Re-alert interval in seconds
- mute: Mute alerts (true/false)
- invert: Invert rule logic (true/false)
- notes: Rule notes
- disabled: Disable rule (0/1)

tools.name: alert_template_create
tools.title: Alert Template Create
tools.description: Create a new alert template in LibreNMS.

payload.description:
Alert template payload fields:
- name (required): Template name
- template (required): Template body (Laravel Blade syntax)
- title (required): Alert title template
- title_rec (required): Recovery title template
- alert_rules (required): Array of alert rule IDs to associate with this template (use [] for none)

LibreNMS renders title, title_rec and template against test data and reads
alert_rules unconditionally, so all five fields must be present. Do not
include template_id: LibreNMS would edit that template instead of creating one.

Example:
{"name": "Custom Alert", "template": "{{ $alert->title }}\nSeverity: {{ $alert->severity }}", "title": "Alert: {{ $alert->title }}", "title_rec": "Recovered: {{ $alert->title }}", "alert_rules": []}

tools.name: alert_template_edit
tools.title: Alert Template Edit
tools.description: Edit an existing alert template in LibreNMS.

payload.description:
Alert template edit payload (must include template_id):
- template_id (required): Integer template ID to edit. Without it LibreNMS would create a
  new template, so the tool refuses the call.
- name (required): Template name
- template (required): Template body (Laravel Blade syntax)
- title (required): Alert title template
- title_rec (required): Recovery title template
- alert_rules (required): Array of alert rule IDs to associate with this template (use [] for none)

LibreNMS replaces the whole template on edit, so resend every field, not just
the ones being changed.

query.description:
Query parameters for filtering devices. Examples:
- {"type": "hostname", "query": "router"} - search by hostname substring
- {"type": "os", "query": "linux"} - filter by operating system
- {"type": "location", "query": "datacenter"} - filter by location

- {"order": "hostname ASC"} - sort results

tools.name: device_add
tools.title: Device Add
tools.description: Add a new device to LibreNMS.

payload.description:
Device add payload. Required and optional fields:
- hostname (required): Device hostname or IP
- version (optional): SNMP version (v1, v2c, v3). Default: v2c
- community (required for v1/v2c): SNMP community string
- authlevel (required for v3): noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv, authPriv
- authname (required for v3): SNMPv3 username
- authpass (required for v3 with auth): Authentication password
- authalgo (optional): MD5 or SHA
- cryptopass (required for authPriv): Privacy password
- cryptoalgo (optional): AES or DES
- port (optional): SNMP port (default: 161)
- transport (optional): udp or tcp
- poller_group (optional): Poller group ID
- force_add (optional): Skip ICMP/SNMP checks (true/false)
- ping_fallback (optional): Add as ping-only if SNMP fails

tools.name: device_graph

tools.description: Render a device-level graph as an image.

graph_type.description: Graph type, as returned by device_graphs_list (e.g. 'device_icmp_perf', 'device_poller_perf', 'device_availability')

from_time.description: Start of the time range, either a relative offset such as '-1d', '-6h' or '-1w', or a Unix timestamp. Defaults to the LibreNMS default (-1d).

to_time.description: End of the time range, either a relative offset or a Unix timestamp. Defaults to now.

legend.description: Whether to render the graph legend.

tools.name: port_graph
tools.title: Port Graph
tools.description:
Render a per-port graph as an image, for example interface traffic.

Names like 'Te2/7' can fail by name behind proxies that reject or decode
the encoded slash. For 'bits' this tool then falls back to the port-group
endpoint, which renders the same traffic data by port ID, so callers
still get a graph.

ifname.description: Interface name as reported by LibreNMS, e.g. 'Po1' or 'Te2/7'

graph_type.description: Graph type: 'bits' (traffic), 'upkts' (unicast packets), 'nupkts' (non-unicast packets), 'errors', or 'etherlike'. The LibreNMS names ('port_bits', ...) are accepted too.

from_time.description: Start of the time range, either a relative offset such as '-1d', '-6h' or '-1w', or a Unix timestamp. Defaults to the LibreNMS default (-1d).

to_time.description: End of the time range, either a relative offset or a Unix timestamp. Defaults to now.

legend.description: Whether to render the graph legend.

tools.name: port_group_graph
tools.title: Port Group Graph
tools.description:
Render a traffic graph for one or more ports, by port ID.

Plots every supplied port on the same axes, which makes it useful for
comparing members of a LAG. Unlike port_graph this takes numeric port
IDs rather than interface names.

port_ids.description: One or more port IDs to plot on a single graph. Resolve names to IDs with ports_search_field or device_ports.

from_time.description: Start of the time range, either a relative offset such as '-1d', '-6h' or '-1w', or a Unix timestamp. Defaults to the LibreNMS default (-1d).

to_time.description: End of the time range, either a relative offset or a Unix timestamp. Defaults to now.

legend.description: Whether to render the graph legend.

tools.name: ports_search_mac
tools.title: Ports Search Mac
tools.description:
Find the switch ports where a MAC address was learned (forwarding table).

This searches LibreNMS's FDB data, i.e. where a host's MAC appears on
the network, not the ports' own hardware addresses: a port's own MAC is
not found unless another device learned it. Results are ordered by how
many MACs each port has learned, so the access port the host is
plugged into usually comes first.

mac.description: MAC address of a host to locate (looked up in the forwarding tables, not ports' own MACs). Accepts aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff, aabb.ccdd.eeff, or aabbccddeeff

tools.name: service_add
tools.title: Service Add
tools.description: Add a service for a device in LibreNMS.

payload.description:
Service monitoring payload:
- type (required): Service check type (e.g., "http", "https", "dns", "ping", "smtp", "ssh", "tcp", "icmp")
- ip (optional): Service IP address or hostname to check (defaults to the device's poller target: its overwrite IP if set, else its hostname)
- desc (optional): Service description
- param (optional): Check parameters/arguments (service-specific)
- ignore (optional): Exclude from alerts (0/1)

Example: {"type": "http", "desc": "Web Server", "param": "-p 8080 -u /health"}

payload.description:

- service_ip: Service IP address
- service_desc: Service description
- service_param: Service check parameters
- service_disabled: 0/1 to enable/disable
- service_ignore: 0/1 to ignore in alerts
